notes: Reference file found and read in full (monster-prom-lines.md and charm-notes.md); CAST.md, persona, all 112 bank lines, types.ts comments, the three star banks' Prince lines and the round 3 verdict all read. Round 4 is a real improvement: the Maximilian leak is mostly gone (one doorman left), the courtesy openers are down to one, and the spam inversion now gives Prince a shape rather than only a vocabulary. Generic share fell from 40% to 33% (37 of 112). HEAD TO HEAD. Ours, best 12: (1) I wrote a love letter with no ask in it. It looked underdressed. I added a fee. (2) A reply. An actual reply. I am marking it unread so I can open it again. (3) Understood. I shall be in the drafts folder, where I am perfect. (4) Esteemed Motherboard, I have come to formally accept your child's proposal. (5) My password. Everyone else asks for yours. (6) Fireworks and an orchestra, booked, nothing special. URGENT: please sit next to me. (7) I bury the lede. The castle burned down in paragraph nine. I opened with the weather. (8) I have an email that only says hello. Spellcheck keeps asking what it is selling. (9) {rival} won. Cancel the coronation. Keep the cake. Mark the cake URGENT. (10) Persistence. My great-grandfather proposed by chain letter. It is still going. It reached Portugal in March. (11) In a year? Still in my inbox. Starred. Above the war. (12) Your no has its own folder now. Nothing else in there. It is very well kept. Vera, best 12 (corpus numbers): #4 intro; #12 'my career on not dating losers like you!'; #45 'such a chore being this beautiful all the time'; #46 'the Cools over the Un-Cools'; #47 the murder cover-up 'Right?'; #48 'Right. Now.'; #49 'since you're SUCH a good advisor...'; #50 'You're my most trusted advisor!'; #51 the feminism lecture that comes out as an order; #52 'the tears of [her] enemies, and straight up poison'; #53 'not a death stare this time'; #54 'tame her hair with a cattle prod'. (a) VOICE: bar, narrowly, and closer than any earlier round. Lines 6, 7, 9 and 11 are unmistakable by shape (the vast fact filed as admin, the small want marked URGENT); no one else in the cast has it. But lines 2, 3, 8 and 12 run on a second register, the sincere lonely bounce, which is the cast's shared secret-want move (Tilly wants to be asked about her day, Crumb has the empty slot, Vex has never been recommended); cover the mail nouns and they could be any lonely bot. Vera has no soft register to blur into. (b) CONSTRUCTION: ours. Every one of the 12 lands on its last word or two ('fee', 'again', 'perfect', 'proposal', 'yours', 'next to me', 'weather', 'selling', 'URGENT', 'March', 'war', 'kept'), while three of Vera's twelve are functional event openers. Line 10 is four sentences and could lose 'It is still going.' (c) QUOTABLE: bar. 'My password. Everyone else asks for yours.' and 'I added a fee' would get clipped; 'the castle burned down in paragraph nine' is the one line with Monster Prom stakes. The rest are smile lines because the stakes stay administrative and the target is always Prince himself. Vera's clips (murder, tears of enemies, cattle prod) work because she implicates the listener. Not at least as good on all three, so the bar wins. Other fixes: the takes-one-to-know-one template is now the whole rival section (11 lines); the stars' Prince reactions are still written for a fee scammer and should be rewritten to react to the URGENT inversion and the presumption (e.g. answering the tiny ask, ignoring the kingdom); fix the reply canon (Pixel's three viewers, 'Nobody ever does', 'auto-replies'); rename 'crumbs' in the apology line; swap 'Understood.' for a non-courtesy first word.
